changelog: Delete C8: remove the broad 'disambiguating stretch' principle because it largely restates concerns already covered by C3 (predicate-argument) and C7 (noun-internal modifiers); pruning this redundant unit reduces overlap so later, targeted edits (e.g. a numeral/unit binding) can act more cleanly on the measured failure modes.
findings: The prompt underrates the harm of cutting where a short following piece (a few words) completes the preceding predicate or provides its essential complement (object, prepositional phrase, date, place, or short clause), producing detached verbs/orphans that break meaning when pieces are translated separately.

The prompt permits cuts inside numeral/measurement spans (numbers, units, parenthetical conversions or multipliers), which severs quantities from their units or clarifying parentheticals and produces contradictory or incoherent translations.

diagnosis.why: Removing C8 eliminated a broad penalty against cutting before a ‘disambiguating stretch’, so the remaining constraints (e.g. predicate-argument and noun-internal rules) drive the model to place earlier/top-level cuts (rank_depth up at k=1,2). That helped very short pieces (bins ≤3–7) but caused more fragmentation of longer post‑modifier/disambiguating spans (bins >10 and overall decline).
diagnosis.lesson: When pruning a broad overlap-removing unit, keep an explicit, targeted safeguard for short disambiguating post-modifier stretches — otherwise the model will cut earlier and fragment longer modifier/PP stretches even as it helps short pieces.

diagnosis.why: Inserting the ordering after C5 caused the model to prefer cutting after short (≤6-word) clausal/complement continuations instead of immediately before them, so many cuts shifted later. That change produced small net losses across all latency bins (by_bin all negative, larger harm for medium/long: ≤7 −0.0088, ≤99 −0.0106) with 1,947 worsened vs 1,790 improved — improvements are concentrated on very short/enumerative pieces while harm occurs when the later cut lands inside or after the following clause (e.g. moves cutting away from 'such as vomiting ‖ are sufficiently general' to a later split inside the predicate).
diagnosis.lesson: Respect that preferring to attach short clausal/complement continuations systematically shifts cuts later and, although it helps some very short/enumerative cases, it degrades medium/long segmentation so it should not be applied unconditionally.
